name: fleet
title: Supgang fleet
description: List this computer and every known Supgang peer with complete signed local and public address candidates. Public scope does not prove reachability.

PathStatistics.description: One QUIC path's congestion and loss state at the time of the read.

black_holes_detected.description: Times MTU discovery found larger packets silently dropped.

congestion_events.description: Times congestion control reduced the window.

congestion_window_bytes.description: Congestion window in bytes: how much may be in flight.

lost_packets.description: QUIC packets declared lost on this path.

sent_packets.description: QUIC packets sent on this path.

PeerConnection.description:
The actual socket used by an authenticated connection at the time of the read.
Counters describe transport activity, not application-level delivery receipts.

path.description:
The QUIC path's measured state, for telling a lossy or policed network
from a transport problem. Absent from older services.

received_datagrams.description: Number of UDP datagrams received on this connection.

remote_address.description: Canonical remote socket, distinct from the peer's advertised candidates.

sent_datagrams.description: Number of UDP datagrams sent on this connection.

connected.description: Live authenticated session state, or absent when read offline.

connection.description: Owner-only live transport diagnostics, not an advertised or durable address.

services.description: Services the computer advertises in its signed record, at its addresses.

tags.description: Local nicknames, never signed by or synchronized with the peer.

report_expires_at.description: Expiry of a short-lived report, when distinct from the endpoint record.

reporter.description: Device that signed a short-lived report, when this is not authoritative endpoint state.

route_compatible.description:
Whether this computer has a compatible address family for an attempt.
This is not a route-table lookup or proof of firewall/router permission.

ServiceRow.description:
One service a computer says it offers, signed by that computer's device.

A claim, not an observation: Supgang has not dialled the port. A consumer
that connects to one of the computer's addresses on `port` and finds a
TLS key whose SHA-256 is `key_pin` is talking to what the computer signed.

key_pin.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the service's TLS public key.

name.description: The service's own name: `dibs`, `remap`, and so on.

port.description: The port it listens on, at the computer's addresses.
